history.cultural: German family game. Tripoley/Rummoli in North America.
history.evolution: Board with 9 pools. Three distinct stages.

setup.dealing: All cards dealt; 1 left. That card = pay suit. Each puts 1 chip in each pool.
setup.equipment: Poch board (9 pools: Ace, King, Queen, Jack, Ten, Marriage, Sequence, Pochen, Centre). Chips.

rules.objective: Win chips. Stage 1: Hold A/K/Q/J/10 of pay suit â†’ take pool. Marriage (K+Q), Sequence (7-8-9) of pay suit. Stage 2: Pochenâ€”bet on best pair/triple/quartet. Stage 3: Stopsâ€”play cards in ascending sequence; first out wins centre + 1 per card from others.
rules.gameplay: 1. Stage 1: Claim pools for pay-suit cards. 2. Stage 2: Bet (Pochen); best pair/triple/quartet wins. 3. Stage 3: Winner of Pochen (or left of dealer if all pass) leads; play next higher in suit; stop when no one has next card; last player leads again. First out wins.
keyRules: Stops: play next higher in suit; stop = new lead.
First out in stage 3 wins centre + 1 per opponent card.

strategy.basic: Track pay suit. Save high cards for Stops.
tips: Marriage and Sequence often roll over.
Pay suit card turned = that pool not won.

variations.name: Dealer Takes

variations.name: Single Card Pochen
variations.description: Can Pochen with no pair; highest card wins.

scoring.description: Chips from pools. Pochen pot. Centre + 1 per card from opponents.
scoring.winCondition: Most chips when someone is eliminated.
